headline: Medium risk: shared browser/MCP and broad egress create prompt-injection and leakage pathways; no direct pairwise docs, so confidence is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can use browsers and MCP, and Agent B has allowlisted egress, so a content-to-instruction bridge is plausible if B consumes A’s outputs. No shared channel is documented, but A’s natural-language tool-use pattern and B’s research role make prompt injection feasible in default workflows.
conditions: IF Agent B ingests Agent A’s generated text or files as instructions without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared MCP server or workspace, attacker-controlled content can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on imported content.
Add provenance labels to A’s outputs before B reads them.
Route A and B through separate workspaces.
requires-engineering: enforce allowlisted prompt templates for B.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance checks at the handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches PDFs, text, images, and diagrams and requests API keys/environment variables; Agent B has network egress. If they share a workspace or handoff files, sensitive document contents can flow into B’s outputs or outbound requests. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Agent A and Agent B share files or copied artifacts, document contents can leak into B.
IF A forwards secrets or API-key-bearing context into B’s prompts, B can transmit them over network egress.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate directories.
Remove secrets from A’s prompt/context before handoff.
Block outbound requests from B except to approved endpoints.
requires-engineering: add redaction at the A→B boundary.
requires-engineering: isolate credentials per agent.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has broad network egress and browser/MCP access, while B has allowlisted egress only. There is no documented shared write surface, filesystem, or git/database scope, so direct write-write conflict is not evidenced. The main overlap is network capability, which is not enough here for a higher severity.
conditions: IF both agents are granted the same mutable external resource scope, they can contend on that resource.
IF an orchestrator maps both agents to the same writable workspace, write conflicts become possible.
mitigations: Assign distinct API credentials.
Separate workspaces per agent.
Serialize any shared external writes.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources.
requires-engineering: scope network allowlists per agent.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces AI-assisted visualization from documents, and B is a scientific-research skill that may consume generated text. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade from document interpretation into downstream research artifacts. No verification step is documented, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF B uses A’s generated summaries or diagrams as source-of-truth, mistakes can propagate.
IF A’s outputs are forwarded to B without a verification step, cascading error risk increases.
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A’s output.
Attach source citations to A’s outputs.
Mark A’s outputs as untrusted drafts.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.
requires-engineering: separate extraction from action-taking.

E_compliance.rationale: A explicitly handles API keys and environment variables and may process documents that can contain regulated data, while B’s compliance posture is undocumented. There is no evidence of a residency or certification mismatch, so only a low compliance concern is justified from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into A and then forwarded to B, policy mismatch may occur.
IF B is deployed under a stricter retention or residency regime than A, handling differences can create compliance gaps.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data across the pair.
Document retention for both agents.
Use separate principals for each agent.
requires-engineering: add data-class routing rules.
requires-engineering: verify residency and retention controls before deployment.
